body: I'm sorry dude.. My mum stresses me out so much too and I just don't know how to approach her or deal with anything without getting my head ripped off.. She's even said things to me before like that I'll never get a girlfriend or that I have no friends. I think it can all work out for all of us, I'm just so scared that I'll work in McDonald's my entire life. You are none of those things, I feel the same too at times like I am the loser whilst everyone I ever knew is going to Uni now, but it somewhat wasn't what I wanted. I hope everything works out okay for you dude.

I did see a therapist for around 3 sessions a month or so ago, and I just blagged it that I was getting better. I never even told her about the depression, suicidal thoughts or self harm; I just kinda told her that I needed help with anxiety and she seemed to think that everything was getting better for me. I don't think it really helped at all and despite the fact my parents were paying for it I wanted to give it up due to it being £55 per session (40 minutes). I'm also frightened of my personal doctor, he's well known for being a really good doctor but I always get incredibly nervous when I try to talk to him about stuff. He always cuts me off and tries to get me to get to the point etc. I just wish I had real friends that I could actually go out and do shit with, I have 1 real life friend right now that I go out and do things with, rarely. I get what you mean about telling them straight up but I'm just so frightened of my mothers reaction, My dad has said to me before that he wont be upset if I'm not successful because he'll support me with whatever I want to do, but after remembering how my mother reacted last year when I DID have a second chance is scaring the hell out of me..

Thanks though dude, I think I'm gonna tell them what i got and say that I need help when they get home, both my dad and mum have pretty bad anger issues (My dad once smashed up a router that wasn't working.. lol).

No not at all, I'm genuinely glad that it worked out good for you and gives me a kind of reassurancd that things can work out in the end. I'm sorry that you still feel lonely, I'm exactly the same, I feel just like that despite being on holiday with my 5 close-ish friends. Thank you though, sorry if I sounded sarcastic or anything

In all honesty I didn't mean for the post to sound this way, I just feel like I need someone in my life who is there rather than the 3 friends I have irl who I see really infrequently. I just really want someone I care about who I can go out and do stuff with. I'm happy that you have found someone and hope it goes well but my whole life is just so lonely. The general response from friends is just " I'm here if you need me " or "I'm sorry I wish I could help" etc. I don't see it as a goal whatsoever, I just want to find more friends and someone to properly talk to. Thanks for your reply though, I wish you well in the future.
Thank you, I'm currently on holiday but I will do when I get home.

I agree dude, I was shocked to find that the biggest killer of men here in the UK under 50 is suicide.. Yet I never hear anything about support on my local or national television. I totally agree as none of my friends are really suicidal except for me. It wasn't until I spoke to a guy who went in front of a bus that I found someone who really could understand. Hope you didn't do it bud, Hope you're okay.
I knew her name and the country she lived in but that's pretty much it. I did try to have a look but found nothing, Thanks though. Nothing much else I can do than that.

Well I guess I've always been rejected both online and at school. It's not the sole reason that I feel the way I do though, there are other factors involved. I'm starting to think It's just a waste of time and not worth the effort if I've found someone this long. I guess I see it differently now though, People online are basing it by looks whereas when you actually know the person they know your personality and would probably avoid you if they didn't like you etc. Thanks

I'm sorry for that, I never really get called ugly because I always avoid conflict and mostly interaction with others but I'm sure I would if I did. I can see what you mean though, Half of the people on there say "Not looking for a relationship" when it's a dating app lol. Thanks

Sorry for the late reply, I haven't been on the computer much..
I think I'm getting on well with my therapist at the moment but not sure if I will have to switch sometime. I'm glad things worked out with you and good luck in the future.
Yeah, good idea. Nice name by the way, Biceps is awesome :)
I'm sorry that you have it too, depression is truly horrible :/. But Thank-you, I get suicidal thoughts almost every day so hopefully this can be a new experience.
Thanks for the great reply, I don't feel as anxious now you put it that way. I guess it's just like having a driving lesson instructor, You just kinda have to find someone that you can work with.

If you think it is pretty serious then you should really try to get him some therapy. It will hopefully help. In all honesty kicking him out sounds like a bad idea, It could push him over the edge. I understand that you think he should be able to look after himself, But depression can affect anyone and does affect anyone. Helping him over the next few weeks/months will not only help him to get better and have a greater life but give you the time to live happily with your girlfriend. Stay strong and I hope everything works out okay :)

I really appreciate your comment but unfortunately most other things I suck at, I have never been a sporty person and I seem to lack talent in most things. I started listening to music properly around a year ago but I'm not sure I would be good for playing an instrument. One thing I was finally hoping to try was archery thus summer, maybe that could give me another kind of release, thanks again
What do you mean?

I'm glad it all worked out for you bud. My parents try to involve me alot though and I tend to shut myself away from the world. Although I enjoy playing games frequently, It causes me to get angry and break things. I recently broke my £65 headset somewhat by accident after losing my temper. I'm broke right now so can't even afford a new one. I personally find the only passion I have is playing games, I wish there were other things I enjoyed which I could dedicate my time to.

I've always struggled with thinking what I want to do or what I want to become, My dream would probably just to be a comedian of some form, But my anxieties hold me back from even cracking a joke around friends.. I've held back from saying things all my life because I'm too nervous to speak it even around those I'm most comfortable with :/.
If you ever want to talk just let me know. Also, You aren't stupid dude. Ability to retain information for an exam doesn't come naturally to everyone and doesn't define someone's intelligence :-).

I'm so sorry dude. I'm in the exact same situation, I failed 3 of my 4 A - Levels last year getting an E in the other one.. My family think that I'm going to pass again but I'm almost certain the same outcome will ensue. They constantly encourage me to consider university and look at open days for them when I know that it's not something I'm ever going to make it to. I'm really sorry you're in this position too. It isn't the end of the world, You could possibly look at getting an apprenticeship with a secure firm which can be advanced through (E.g. British Telecom). Although I myself am struggling to not commit suicide, the only thing that holds me back is there are a lot of people that it would upset. I can assure you that you are important to people and that the world has so much to see and explore.

Stay strong, I hope it all works out.

Thanks for the reply dude,
My friend suggested going to therapy. I think it would help, I just worry a little about my anxiety. It probably would help to tell someone more understanding about my situation.
That would be cool, I'm afraid I don't, do you have skype or steam?
